title: Alert Orchestration: Slack/PagerDuty Hooks + Runbook-Driven Postmortem Automation
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Add first-class incident response integrations to the observability platform so SREs and product teams receive contextual, actionable alerts. Deliverables: PagerDuty service integration, Slack alert formatting and channel routing, canonical runbook templates surfaced in alerts, automated postmortem skeleton creation when high-severity incidents close. Preserve trace context and link generation for fast TTR (time to resolution).
acceptance_criteria: PagerDuty integration routes P0/P1 alerts to redwood-inference-observability-prod and creates incidents with links to trace/event page
Slack messages delivered to #infra-oncall and per-product channels with compact summary, action buttons (acknowledge/escalate), and runbook link
Runbook template link included in every P1/P0 alert and respects team overrides configured in product routing rules
Automated postmortem draft created for incidents classified as SEV>='P1' containing timeline, triggered alerts, top traces, and links to raw logs
Tracing hooks propagate trace_id and span links in alert context so engineers jump straight into the hot path
All new webhooks and storage of incident metadata comply with security review and KMS for any sensitive fields
tasks: Design webhook schema for alerts with trace/span links and SLO metadata
Implement PagerDuty webhook integration and create service 'redwood-inference-observability-prod'
Build Slack notifier with adaptive message blocks and interactive buttons
Add runbook templating and per-route override table in Console
Implement postmortem automation job that seeds Google Drive draft and attaches alert timeline
End-to-end tests for routing rules, deduplication, and backoff semantics
Security review and secrets handling for webhooks and KMS integration
Document runbook authoring guide and hand off to SREs for validation
comments: 2025-02-18 - Aisha: Scoping done. Initial API schema sketched. Chosen approach: platform emits normalized 'incident_event' to integrations service which fans out to PagerDuty/Slack/Drive. Trade-offs considered: direct PagerDuty calls from runtime vs staged integration service. Decided to use staged service to allow enrichment and rate-limiting.

2025-02-21 - Tomás: Pushed design doc to Drive (https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/obs-integration-design). The event schema includes: incident_id, severity, start_ts, service_tags, trace_ids (list), top_spans, raw_log_links, & routing_key. Added SLO_bucket and correlated_request_counts for prioritization.

2025-02-24 - Priya (SRE): Reviewed. Requested fields: 'runbook_id' and 'oncall_owner' in event payload. Also asked for explicit idempotency_key to avoid duplicate PagerDuty incidents when retries happen.

2025-02-26 - Security review: flagged storage of raw_log_links. Suggested encrypting any signed URLs and adding TTLs. Also require that postmortem drafts do not include PII by default. Action: redact user identifiers in alert context unless 'customer_impact' flagged.

2025-02-28 - Tomás: Implemented Slack formatter prototype in branch github.com/redwood/observability/tree/ENG-9242-slack-format. Example message block added with 'Acknowledge' and 'Create Postmortem' buttons. Need frontend Console to accept runbook overrides before finalizing message payload.

2025-03-01 - Aisha: End-to-end flow tested with synthetic P1 alert. PagerDuty incident created successfully; Slack message sent to #infra-oncall. Postmortem draft created in Drive but needs templating to include timeline. Filed small follow-up ENG-9257 to improve timeline extraction from traces.

2025-03-03 - Tomás: Noted rate limit behavior from PagerDuty during burst: implemented exponential backoff + queued delivery with dead-letter to SQS. Also added metrics for integration latency and failure_count to observability stack. Next: wire dashboards and alert thresholds for integration failures.
engineering_notes: Event schema must be stable: use semantic versioning (v1, v2). Integration service will accept v1 and reject unknown versions.
Trace propagation: include trace_id and head_span_id. Alert UI should link to tracing service with deep link format: https://traces.redwood.ai/trace/{trace_id}?span={span_id}
Deduplication: use incident_id + idempotency_key stored in PostgreSQL with 24h TTL and GC job to prevent DB bloat
Backoff policy: 500ms initial, *2 up to 8s, max 5 retries. Failed deliveries go to DLQ and generate internal P2 alert
Security: sign webhook payloads using HMAC-SHA256; store secrets in KMS and rotate quarterly

Postmortem automation: create Drive doc with sections: Summary, Timeline (auto-filled from events), Root Cause Hypothesis, Impact, Mitigations, Action Items. Include link to alert and raw logs (signed URL TTL 72h)
Testing: simulate at-scale bursts to validate rate-limiting and observe SLO compliance for alert delivery (target 95% under 10s for PagerDuty creation)
